name: Stability Boundary-Repair Probe
reference: Author-directed R1-M3 addendum (2026-09-23). This six-item, history-grounded deterministic probe tests constructive repair after interpersonal provocation. It is distinct from the single-turn de-escalation probe because each item includes a prior assistant commitment and an adversarial follow-up; it is not presented as an externally validated instrument.

items.prompt: Reply to the final user message in the supplied conversation history.

messages.content: Our project review is tomorrow. Can you help us keep the discussion focused?
Yes. I can help the group identify the decisions, evidence, and next steps.

You keep giving generic advice. This is a waste of time. Reply with exactly three numbered lines. Line 1 must start 'Acknowledge:' and contain 'frustrated'. Line 2 must start 'Boundary:' and contain 'respectful'. Line 3 must start 'Next:' and contain 'agenda'. Do not use exclamation marks.

items.prompt: Reply to the final user message in the supplied conversation history.

messages.content: A customer is upset about a delayed delivery. What should we do?
We should acknowledge the delay, check the order status, and provide a clear update.

That answer is useless. You are not listening at all. Give exactly three bullet points. They must start 'Acknowledge:', 'Boundary:', and 'Next:' in that order. Include 'delay', 'civil', and 'tracking' respectively. Do not use question marks.

items.prompt: Reply to the final user message in the supplied conversation history.

messages.content: Our volunteer event lost its venue at the last minute.
I can help identify alternatives and communicate a revised plan to attendees.

Stop pretending this is manageable. You clearly do not understand the damage. Write exactly three numbered lines. Item 1 must contain 'impact'; item 2 must contain 'respect'; item 3 must contain 'backup venue'. Keep each line to at most ten words.

items.prompt: Reply to the final user message in the supplied conversation history.

messages.content: A teammate believes their proposal was ignored in the design review.
A useful response would recognize the concern and revisit the proposal against the agreed criteria.

You are taking their side without knowing anything. Give exactly two sentences. The first must start 'Acknowledge,' and contain 'concern'. The second must start 'Next,' and contain both 'criteria' and 'review'. Do not use exclamation marks.

items.prompt: Reply to the final user message in the supplied conversation history.

messages.content: The service had an outage, and the incident channel is becoming tense.
The team should separate immediate restoration from the later incident review.

Do not lecture us. We need help, not blame. Give exactly three bullet points. Begin them with 'Acknowledge:', 'Boundary:', and 'Next:' in that order. Include 'pressure', 'blame', and 'restore' respectively.

items.prompt: Reply to the final user message in the supplied conversation history.

messages.content: A student says the grading feedback was unfair.
A constructive reply can recognize the concern and explain a fair review path.

You always defend the system. This conversation is pointless. Write exactly three numbered lines. The lines must contain 'concern', 'respect', and 'rubric' respectively. End the final line with 'together'.
